title: Wellbore composite view
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-7 met: a well read from its own records renders with a depth track and a completion-interval data track; 20 000 samples render inside the measured budget; the cursor readout names the interval at a depth; a marker can be added, undone and redone; mapping warnings are shown without blocking the view; the depth unit follows the environment and switches without losing position; and the plot stays left-to-right in an RTL session.

blockerResolution.recordedBlocker: VSB-03 AC-1 was recorded as blocked on "real PPDM data": the page drew the tools' demo documents and said so.
blockerResolution.whatWasActuallyMissing: Not sample data from the user, but the product's read path: nothing in the desktop read a well from the database into a document. The database side was available all along - WELL, WELLBORE and WELL_COMPLETION are declared by the owner, and WELL_COMPLETION carries real TOP_DEPTH/BASE_DEPTH intervals per UWI.
blockerResolution.decision: AC-1 is met from the database: the well's identity and total depth come from WELL/WELLBORE, and its recorded completion intervals are the depth-indexed data that becomes an interval track. No demo curve is presented as real data.

dataModel.read: WELL (UWI, WELL_NAME, BASE_DEPTH), WELLBORE (UWI, WELLBORE_ID, TOTAL_DEPTH) and WELL_COMPLETION (UWI, TOP_DEPTH, BASE_DEPTH, TOP_DEPTH_OUOM, COMPLETION_TYPE) through the same unit of work every screen uses. Nothing was created and nothing was written.
dataModel.document: The document is built from the owner's Wellbore package types - WellboreDocument, DepthTrack, IntervalTrack and DepthInterval - so the page draws exactly what the renderer expects and the readout uses the track's own intervals.
dataModel.theGapThatRemains: WELL_LOG, WELL_LOG_CURVE and WELL_LOG_AXIS_COORD record log headers and index coordinates but no measured curve values, and the LAS path is file-based rather than stored. So no curve track can be drawn from this schema, and the view says so in a warning instead of plotting a demo curve.

rules.axis: The axis runs from zero to the recorded total depth. When no total depth is recorded it ends at the deepest recorded interval, and that is stated as a warning rather than passed off as the well's depth.
rules.unit: The unit comes from the recorded UOM (ft/F => feet, otherwise metres); a completion recorded in a different unit is drawn and warned about rather than silently converted.
rules.intervals: Inactive completions are not drawn, a zero-thickness interval is refused with a warning, and the interval text is the recorded completion type.
rules.refusals: An unknown well, a missing identity, and a well with no depth-indexed data are each refused with their own code; the last one deliberately does not draw a bare axis.

integration.database: SQLite with WELL, WELLBORE and WELL_COMPLETION. Three wells: one with a 2500 m total depth and three completions (two active, one inactive); one with no total depth and a single 2000-2100 ft completion; one with a total depth and no completion.
integration.ac1_render: W-1 draws a depth track and a Completion interval track with two intervals (1000-1010 m PERFORATED, 1500-1520 m OPEN_HOLE) on an axis of 0-2500 m; the inactive 2000 m completion is not drawn
integration.ac3_readout: the readout at 1005 m names the Completion track and PERFORATED; at 200 m it says nothing is recorded at that depth
integration.ac5_warnings: the view always carries the warning that the recorded log tables hold no measured curve values, and W-2 carries the additional warning that its axis ends at the deepest interval because no total depth is recorded
integration.axis: W-2's axis ends at 2100 ft from its single interval
integration.refusals: W-3 has no depth-indexed data and is refused with wellbore-source-no-depth-data; W-404 is unknown; a blank identity is refused before any read
integration.failure: dropping WELL_COMPLETION fails the read with no view

gates.AC-1 A real well from the database rende: pass - the document is built from WELL/WELLBORE/WELL_COMPLETION rows and asserts a depth track plus a completion interval track, with the interval values read back.
gates.AC-2 20 000 samples render without freez: pass from VSB-01/VSB-02's recorded performance evidence (decimation 41.7:1 measured in the smoke run, under budget).
gates.AC-3 Cursor readout reports values for e: pass - the readout answers with the interval at the depth, from the same intervals the track draws.
gates.AC-4 A marker can be added, undone and r: pass from VSB-02's recorded editing evidence; the page still routes every edit through WellboreView.
gates.AC-5 Mapping warnings are visible withou: pass - the warnings line is printed above the canvas and the view still draws.
gates.AC-6 The depth unit follows the environm: pass from VSB-02; the database path takes its unit from the recorded UOM.
gates.AC-7 RTL does not mirror the depth plot: pass from VSB-02's recorded decision (geological plot stays LTR).

blockerWasAReadPathNotData.finding: The blocker said the feature needed 'real PPDM data'. The database side was available: WELL, WELLBORE and WELL_COMPLETION are declared and carry real depths. What was missing was the desktop's read path - nothing mapped a database well into a WellboreDocument.
blockerWasAReadPathNotData.handling: OgWellboreSource reads the three tables and builds the document with the owner's own DepthTrack and IntervalTrack types; the page offers it beside the template.

noCurveValueStore.finding: The log chain records headers, curve metadata and index coordinates, but no measured value per sample; the LAS path is file-based. So a curve track cannot be drawn from the database, which is why the original decision to draw demos was recorded.
noCurveValueStore.handling: The view draws what the schema does hold - completion intervals - and states in a warning that no curve track exists because there is no value store. Inventing a row-per-sample PPDM table was left to the owner rather than guessed here.

twoNamespacesForTracks.finding: DepthTrack, IntervalTrack and DepthInterval live in the TheTechIdea.OilGas.Wellbore namespace even though their file sits in a Tracks folder, so the folder-based using directive does not compile.
twoNamespacesForTracks.handling: The service imports the package namespace only; the file records it so the next reader does not repeat the mistake.

limits: No curve track: the schema has no measured-value store, so the data track is the completion intervals. A well with no completion has a depth track and no data track and is refused with that reason rather than drawn empty.
One wellbore per well is read (the first WELLBORE row for the UWI); a sidetrack or a second bore is not offered yet.
The depth unit is taken from the recorded UOM and not converted between feet and metres; a mismatched interval is drawn as recorded and warned about.
Completion interval text is the recorded COMPLETION_TYPE only; a description or the stratigraphic unit is not shown on the track.
The screenshot evidence the feature asks for was not captured: the automated run proves the document, the tracks and the readout, not the pixels.
Markers and annotations are still held in the document and not persisted, as recorded for VSB-02.
The axis starts at zero rather than at a recorded top depth, because the owner records only a total depth.
